title: Outer-2 real-SWAP participant admissibility boundary at the solver-configuration split
question: At the frozen outer-2 G11/G17 carrier, why does a head displacement of only about 2e-13 m around the independent G17 response root flip the real FMR/SWAP participant from status 0 to status 6, and is that status boundary deterministic, monotone and execution-diagnostically resolvable?
purpose: Characterize the local participant-admissibility topology before interpreting solver-configuration path differences as coupling robustness. This is a diagnostic boundary-resolution unit, not an acceptance-policy change.
experiment_contract: Initialize the same real FGC44 carrier and immutable FMR origin used by G17/G21E.
Begin a fresh G16 session and verify the three frozen anchor heads reproduce their persisted participant statuses before any boundary inference.
Scan 33 unique ordered binary64 heads spanning the closed NOUR-status6 to G17-status0 bracket; record status, q availability and all G15 execution diagnostics.

Require the coarse bracket statuses to be monotone from status 6 on the more-negative side to status 0 on the less-negative side before applying binary search. Any status island or reversal yields NONMONOTONE_OR_UNRESOLVED and no single threshold claim.
If monotone, bisect in binary64 head space until the status-6 lower endpoint and status-0 upper endpoint are adjacent representable floating-point values or no further distinct midpoint exists.
Record the final boundary width in metres and in binary64 ulps around the transition.
Probe the final lower/upper endpoints and the nearest four representable neighbours on both sides; retain complete participant observation diagnostics.

End the session, begin two additional fresh G16 sessions from the same immutable accepted origin, and repeat the final neighbourhood probes to test cross-session determinism with fresh physical participant trials.
All diagnostic candidates remain discarded through G16. Accepted revision/time, ledger state, FMR preflight and ledger preflight must remain unchanged throughout.
Do not alter solver tolerances, SWAP numerical configuration, head values, participant status semantics or trial retry policy.
quantitative_gates: Frozen G17 head reproduces status 0; frozen NOUR lambda=1 head reproduces status 6; frozen STANDARD head reproduces status 0.
All 33 coarse scan heads are unique binary64 values and return only status 0 or 6.
Report transition count in the ordered coarse scan; exactly one transition is required for a MONOTONE_SINGLE_BOUNDARY classification.
For a monotone bracket, final status-6 and status-0 endpoints are adjacent representable binary64 values or midpoint exhaustion is demonstrated.
The final bracket endpoints retain their status in all three independent G16 sessions.

Report participant result status, completed, candidate_ready, attempts, retries, solver_rejections, temporal_rejections, temporal_unavailable_rejections, mass_rejections, internal_retries and accepted-substep range for every final-neighbour probe.
Report whether any execution-diagnostic field changes before the status flip and identify the first field differences across the adjacent boundary endpoints.
No ordinary publication-path trial is used and no accepted state, ledger or preflight authority changes.

interpretation_rules.MONOTONE_SINGLE_BOUNDARY: Coarse scan has exactly one 6-to-0 transition, binary64 bisection resolves one adjacent status-6/status-0 pair, and the boundary statuses reproduce across all three fresh sessions.
interpretation_rules.NONMONOTONE_OR_UNRESOLVED: The bracket contains status islands/reversals, unexpected statuses, nondeterministic repeats, or cannot maintain the frozen endpoint statuses.
interpretation_rules.DETERMINISTIC_EXECUTION_THRESHOLD: MONOTONE_SINGLE_BOUNDARY plus a reproducible discrete change in execution diagnostics across the adjacent endpoints. This labels an execution-level threshold only; it does not identify the physical or source-level cause.
interpretation_rules.DETERMINISTIC_STATUS_BOUNDARY_CAUSE_UNRE: MONOTONE_SINGLE_BOUNDARY but the available diagnostics do not localize the cause of the status flip.

pass_interpretation: PASS means the local status topology and repeatability were measured without changing participant semantics. A deterministic one-ulp boundary is diagnostic evidence, not justification for loosening status 6 or adding a head tolerance.
fail_interpretation: Preserve failures. Do not smooth, snap, round, perturb or widen head acceptance after seeing the boundary; do not reinterpret status 6 as admissible.
